human_tolerance.notes: Regularly works feeders, usually taking one seed and flying to a branch isolated from other birds to eat it; it stores seeds for later use and is permanent resident rather than migratory.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Winter flocks hold ranks: in spring the highest-ranked birds keep the flock's territory to breed and lower-ranked birds must find new ground.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Judgement: the article gives clutches of three to ten eggs, 12-16 days of incubation and a 16-19 day nestling period but dates no season, so early spring to midsummer is authored.

vocalizations.description: A four-note see-dee-see-dee song, which separates it from the two- or three-note song of the black-capped chickadee; where the two meet they can mimic each other's songs.

The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, faster and higher-pitched than the black-capped chickadee's. Chickadees call out whenever they find a good source of food, which is what holds a mixed winter flock together.
A gargle call made by the dominant bird when another bird encroaches on its individual space of 2-5 ft; rates are higher in high-quality foraging habitats.

common_names.note: French from Wikidata; German and Dutch from the GBIF vernacular-name list, which Wikidata does not carry for this species.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005). The article describes the species as largely found in the southeastern and central United States, without a status statement.

range.note: 'mixed or deciduous forests in the United States from New Jersey and Pennsylvania west to southern Kansas and south to Florida and Texas', with a gap at high altitude in the Appalachians. It hybridises with the black-capped chickadee where the ranges overlap.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Carolina chickadees hop along tree branches searching for insects, sometimes hanging upside down or hovering; they may make short flights to catch insects in the air.'

traits.nest_type.note: 'The Carolina chickadee nests in a hole in a tree; mating pairs excavate the nest, using a natural cavity or sometimes an old woodpecker nest.'

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement, not sourced. No openly licensed source used in this record gives a longevity figure for the Carolina chickadee, and the Wikipedia article gives none. 6 years is an authored placeholder on the scale of a small parid and should be treated as unverified; a banded wild bird is very unlikely to reach it.

traits.diet.note: 'Insects form a large part of their diet, especially in summer; seeds and berries become important in winter.' The 60/25/15 split is judgement inside those bounds.

traits.social.note: 'During the winter, chickadees often flock together. Each of the birds in a flock has a rank', and mixed flocks with titmice, nuthatches and warblers occur about half the time.

traits.defense.note: Withdraws to cover and garrles at an encroaching dominant; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Tame at feeders and described as a non-migratory permanent resident, though it eats away from other birds on an isolated branch.

habitat.use.note: 'hop along tree branches searching for insects, sometimes hanging upside down or hovering'; almost entirely in the canopy and understory.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: 'These birds usually sleep in cavities, though they may sleep in branches. Different members of a flock will sleep in the same cavity from night to night.'

habitat.resources.note: Food weights and their months follow traits.diet and the diet sentence's seasonal emphasis; nest sites from the breeding description.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'At feeders, these birds will usually take a seed and fly to a branch isolated from other birds to eat it', and they hammer and store seeds.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'They are permanent residents, not usually moving south even in severe winter weather.'

seasonal.phases.note: Winter flock ranking and its effect on which birds breed are described. The nesting window is authored: the article gives clutch and incubation figures but no calendar dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 12-16 days of incubation plus a 16-19 day nestling period gives about 34 days; the 0.7 scale is authored judgement.

look.note: Black cap and bib, white sides to the face, grey back, rusty brown flanks, a short dark bill and a moderately long tail, from the Description section; the cap and bib are extra parts and the proportions are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag invertebrate because insects dominate the summer diet and the flock's cohesion call is about finding them; flee_m 5 m is short because the bird drops to cover rather than flying far. The alarm slot uses the documented gargle call.
